newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish toymaker Lego to launch new product line.
newsitem.headline: Danish toymaker Lego to launch new product line.

text.p: Danish toymaker Lego on Wednesday unveiled a range of fresh products aimed at attracting more girls after 65 years of boy-dominated sales of its building bricks and accessories.

The new Lego Scala range applies the build-it-yourself principle to dolls' houses while new additions to the Belville line include a riding school, a pony-trekking set and a circus princess, a Lego statement said.
"Lego Scala is a completely new, flexible dolls' house system capable of infinite variation. Girls can decide for themselves its structure and furnishing," it said.
"The different dolls' houses, surroundings and contents can be mixed, adapted and added to, according to a girl's imagination," the statement added.

It said that the range of 10 different Scala sets, priced from about 70 to 1,000 Danish crowns, would be launched in Denmark, Switzerland, Sweden, Germany and Austria in March and in France in September.
As well as the houses themselves the sets offer furnishings, accessories and figures of parents, children and pets.
"There is a warm and friendly atmosphere with the family at the centre," Lego said,

The company, the only European firm among the world's top 10 toymakers, reported profits down by 50 percent in 1995 compared to the year before and blamed competition from computer games as a factor in falling sales.
To strike back Lego is adding a CD-ROM disc to its Lego Technic range for older children.

The disc -- compatible with both Windows and Macintosh systems -- will combine animated step-by-step building instructions for a submarine and "mobile underwater base" with background facts on underwater life and submarine dives. When a model is completed its builder can print a personalised diploma. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969652
